### 2.3 Cleaning and updating attribute fields of the geospatial data



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
eldercare <- eldercare %>%
  select(fid, ADDRESSPOS) %>%
  mutate(capacity = 100)
```
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
hexagons <- hexagons %>%
  select(fid) %>%
  mutate(demand = 100)
```
:::



## 3. Apsaital Data Handling and Wrangling

### 3.1 Importing Distance Matrix



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ODMatrix <- read_csv("data/aspatial/OD_Matrix.csv", skip = 0)
```
:::



### 3.2 Tidying distance matrix



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
distmat <- ODMatrix %>%
  select(origin_id, destination_id, total_cost) %>%
  spread(destination_id, total_cost)%>%
  select(c(-c('origin_id')))
```
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
distmat_km <- as.matrix(distmat/1000)
```
:::



## 4. Modelling and Visualising Accessibility using Hansen Method

### 4.1 Computing Hansen’s accessibility



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
acc_Hansen <- data.frame(ac(hexagons$demand,
                            eldercare$capacity,
                            distmat_km, 
                            #d0 = 50,
                            power = 2, 
                            family = "Hansen"))
```
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
colnames(acc_Hansen) <- "accHansen"
```
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
acc_Hansen <- as_tibble(acc_Hansen)
```
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
hexagon_Hansen <- bind_cols(hexagons, acc_Hansen)
```
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
acc_Hansen <- data.frame(ac(hexagons$demand,
                            eldercare$capacity,
                            distmat_km, 
                            #d0 = 50,
                            power = 0.5, 
                            family = "Hansen"))

colnames(acc_Hansen) <- "accHansen"
acc_Hansen <- as_tibble(acc_Hansen)
hexagon_Hansen <- bind_cols(hexagons, acc_Hansen)
```
:::



### Hansen accessibility for all powers (0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5)



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
powers <- c(0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5)

acc_list <- lapply(powers, function(p) {
  x <- data.frame(ac(hexagons$demand,
                     eldercare$capacity,
                     distmat_km,
                     power = p,
                     family = "Hansen"))
  colnames(x) <- paste0("accHansen_", p)
  as_tibble(x)
})

# Binding all accessibility columns to hexagons
hexagon_Hansen_all <- bind_cols(hexagons, acc_list)
```
:::



### 4.2 Visualising Hansen’s accessibility

#### 4.2.1 Extracting map extend



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
mapex <- st_bbox(hexagons)
```
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tm_shape(hexagon_Hansen,
         bbox = mapex) + 
  tm_polygons(fill = "accHansen", 
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(
                style = "quantile",
                n = 10,
                values = "brewer.blues")) +
tm_shape(eldercare) +
  tm_dots(size = 0.3,
          fill = "red",
          col = "black") +
  tm_title("Accessibility to eldercare: Hansen method") +
  tm_layout(frame = TRUE) +
  tm_compass(type="8star", size = 2) +
  tm_scalebar() +
  tm_grid(alpha = 0.2)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](In-class_Ex09_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-20-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::



#### Comparison map for all Hansen power values



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
mapex <- st_bbox(hexagons)

vars <- c("accHansen_0.5",
          "accHansen_1",
          "accHansen_1.5",
          "accHansen_2",
          "accHansen_2.5")

titles <- c("Power 0.5",
            "Power 1",
            "Power 1.5",
            "Power 2",
            "Power 2.5")

for (i in seq_along(vars)) {
  print(
    tm_shape(hexagon_Hansen_all, bbox = mapex) +
      tm_polygons(vars[i],
                  style = "quantile",
                  n = 10,
                  palette = "Blues",
                  title = "Hansen Accessibility") +
      tm_shape(eldercare) +
      tm_dots(size = 0.3, col = "red") +
      tm_layout(title = titles[i],
                frame = TRUE)
  )
}
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](In-class_Ex09_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-21-1.png){width=672}
:::

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](In-class_Ex09_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-21-2.png){width=672}
:::

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](In-class_Ex09_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-21-3.png){width=672}
:::

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](In-class_Ex09_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-21-4.png){width=672}
:::

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](In-class_Ex09_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-21-5.png){width=672}
:::
:::



Centralization/Decentralization: The areas of highest accessibility (darkest blue) change.

-   Low Power (0.5): The map shows the least centralized pattern. High accessibility spreads out more across the island. The effect of distance is less severe, meaning locations far from the center still get a significant score contribution from opportunities. The overall range of accessibility values is the highest (up to 1,157.6).

-   High Power (2.0 to 2.5): The map shows the most centralized/localized pattern. The high accessibility areas are very tightly clustered around the locations of the opportunities (the black dots). Distance acts as a strong deterrent, so only cells very close to an opportunity receive a high score. Accessibility drops off quickly in surrounding areas. The overall range of accessibility values is the lowest, and the absolute values are much smaller.

    | Power | Distance Deterrence | Accessibility Pattern | Key Observation |
    |------------|--------------|----------------------|-----------------------------|
    | 0.5 | Weak | Diffuse/Decentralized | Highest overall scores; high accessibility extends far from opportunities. |
    | 1.0 | Moderate | Smoother Gradient | Balance between distance and opportunity size; high scores still relatively widespread. |
    | 2.0 - 2.5 | Strong | Localized/Centralized | Lowest overall scores; high accessibility is strictly limited to cells immediately adjacent to opportunities. |

### 4.3 Statistical graphic visualisation



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
hexagon_Hansen <- st_join(hexagon_Hansen, mpsz, 
                          join = st_intersects)
```
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(data=hexagon_Hansen, 
       aes(y = log(accHansen), 
           x= REGION_N)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_point(stat="summary", 
             fun.y="mean", 
             colour ="red", 
             size=2)
```

## 6. Modelling and Visualising Accessibility using Spatial Accessibility Measure (SAM) Method

### 6.1 Computing SAM accessibility



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
acc_SAM <- data.frame(ac(hexagons$demand,
                         eldercare$capacity,
                         distmat_km, 
                         d0 = 5,
                         power = 2, 
                         family = "SAM"))

colnames(acc_SAM) <- "accSAM"
acc_SAM <- as_tibble(acc_SAM)
hexagon_SAM <- bind_cols(hexagons, acc_SAM)
```
:::



### 6.2 Visualising SAM’s accessibility

```{.r .cell-code}
tm_shape(eldercare) +
  tm_dots(size = 0.3,
          fill = "red",
          col = "black") +
  tm_title("Accessibility to eldercare: SAM method") +
  tm_layout(frame = TRUE) +
```

```{.r .cell-code}
# Comparing all three methods in one layout

tmap_mode("plot")
# Disabling automatic resizing and accept potential overlap/clipping
# tmap_options(component.autoscale = FALSE)

tm1 <- tm_shape(hexagon_Hansen) +
  tm_polygons("accHansen", style = "quantile", n = 5, palette = "brewer.blues") +
  tm_layout(title = "Hansen Accessibility")

tm2 <- tm_shape(hexagon_KD2SFCA) +
  tm_polygons("accKD2SFCA", style = "quantile", n = 5, palette = "brewer.greens") +
  tm_layout(title = "KD2SFCA Accessibility")

tm3 <- tm_shape(hexagon_SAM) +
  tm_polygons("accSAM", style = "quantile", n = 5, palette = "brewer.purples") +
  tm_layout(title = "SAM Accessibility")

tmap_arrange(tm1, tm2, tm3, ncol = 3)
```
